stem: An asymptomatic 32-year-old adult has obesity, is physically inactive, and has a parent with type 2 diabetes. Which action best reflects current diabetes screening guidance?

options.A: Screen for prediabetes or type 2 diabetes now because overweight or obesity plus additional risk factors warrants testing even before age 35.
options.B: Wait until age 35 because risk factors do not change the age at which testing should begin.
options.C: Do not screen unless classic hyperglycemia symptoms develop because testing asymptomatic adults is not recommended.
options.D: Screen only if the client first develops hypertension because family history and physical inactivity are not recognized risk factors.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care recommend risk assessment in asymptomatic adults and advise testing adults of any age who have overweight or obesity plus at least one additional risk factor. Recognized factors include a first-degree relative with diabetes and physical inactivity, among others. For people who do not otherwise meet risk-based criteria, routine screening begins at age 35. B incorrectly treats age 35 as a minimum regardless of risk. C and D ignore current risk-based screening guidance.
educational_objective: Apply risk-based diabetes screening by testing asymptomatic adults before age 35 when overweight or obesity is accompanied by additional recognized risk factors such as first-degree family history or physical inactivity.
source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
source_document_title: Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
source_locator: Recommendations 2.11, 2.12a–2.12c and Table 2.5 — assess diabetes risk in asymptomatic adults; consider testing at any age in adults with overweight or obesity plus one or more risk factors including first-degree family history and physical inactivity; for all others screening begins at age 35
source_claim_supported: Current ADA guidance supports diabetes testing before age 35 when an asymptomatic adult has overweight/obesity plus at least one recognized risk factor, including first-degree family history or physical inactivity.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — assess risk factors and reinforce age- and risk-appropriate preventive screening
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — risk-based screening for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source risk-factor-list item into an application-level screening decision. The final version uses current ADA 2026 criteria and avoids presenting race/ethnicity as a standalone deterministic trait or implying that age is the only meaningful screening trigger.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.clinical_category: prediabetes/type 2 diabetes screening / adult risk assessment
audit_findings.source_audit: Verified directly against ADA Standards of Care 2026 Section 2 and Table 2.5. The any-age risk-based screening rule and listed family-history/physical-inactivity factors are explicit.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: The stem provides obesity plus two recognized risk factors in an asymptomatic adult younger than 35, making early screening directly supported. No laboratory threshold or screening test is unnecessarily specified.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; the client meets current risk-based testing criteria before age 35.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; age 35 is the general starting age for those who do not already meet risk-based criteria.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; asymptomatic adults are specifically included in screening recommendations.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; family history and physical inactivity are already recognized risk factors.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A correctly applies the current risk-based screening framework.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address timing/eligibility for diabetes screening.
audit_findings.blueprint: Health Promotion and Maintenance is appropriate because the construct is preventive risk assessment and screening.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked age-35 rule, overweight/obesity prerequisite for any-age adult risk-based testing, family-history definition, physical-inactivity factor, symptom-independent screening, and second-answer risk. No unresolved conflict remained.
